data.definition: Able or likely to cause harm or injury.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'dangerous for' or 'dangerous to' when identifying the vulnerable target.
examples: Walking alone late at night can be dangerous for tourists.
Toxic fumes are dangerous to human health.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Extreme sports are dangerous with beginners. ➜ ✅ Extreme sports are dangerous for beginners.

data.definition: Refusing to listen to or consider advice or requests.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'deaf to' figuratively when someone refuses to listen.
examples: The administration remained deaf to the employees' grievances.
He was deaf to all warnings.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He was deaf for my advice. ➜ ✅ He was deaf to my advice.

data.definition: Devoted to a task or purpose; having single-minded loyalty.
data.grammar_rule: Follow 'dedicated to' with a noun or gerund (-ing).
examples: The monument is dedicated to fallen soldiers.
She is dedicated to serving her community.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is dedicated to help others. ➜ ✅ He is dedicated to helping others.

data.definition: Relying on someone or something for support, help, or supply.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'on' or 'upon' after 'dependent'.
examples: The country's economy is heavily dependent on oil exports.
Young children are dependent on their parents.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It is dependent from the weather. ➜ ✅ It is dependent on the weather.

data.definition: Obtained or formed from a primary source.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'from' after 'derived'.
examples: Many English words are derived from Latin and Greek roots.
Aspirin was originally derived from willow bark.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The drug is derived of plants. ➜ ✅ The drug is derived from plants.

data.definition: Tending to cause harm or damage.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'detrimental'. Never use 'for'.
examples: Lack of sleep is detrimental to mental performance.
High tariffs proved detrimental to international trade.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Pollution is detrimental for wildlife. ➜ ✅ Pollution is detrimental to wildlife.

data.definition: Entirely lacking or free from something desirable.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'devoid'.
examples: The landscape was desolate and completely devoid of life.
His voice was devoid of emotion during the interview.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The room was devoid from furniture. ➜ ✅ The room was devoid of furniture.

data.definition: Not the same as another person or thing.
data.grammar_rule: 'Different from' is standard across British and American English. 'Different to' is common in British English, and 'different than' is used informally in American English.
examples: Living in a small town is very different from living in a big city.
His opinion is completely different from mine.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Life here is different of my home country. ➜ ✅ Life here is different from my home country.

data.definition: Sad or displeased because expectations were not fulfilled.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'disappointed in/with' a person or character. Use 'disappointed at/about' a outcome, decision, or result.
examples: His parents were deeply disappointed in his dishonesty.
We were disappointed at the match result.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I am disappointed from the film. ➜ ✅ I am disappointed with the film.

data.definition: Too large or too small in comparison with something else.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'disproportionate'.
examples: The harsh punishment was disproportionate to the minor offense.
He spends a disproportionate amount of time on administrative tasks.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The response was disproportionate with the threat. ➜ ✅ The response was disproportionate to the threat.

data.definition: Hesitating or doubting; not to be relied upon.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'dubious about' or 'dubious of'.
examples: Economists are dubious about the feasibility of the proposal.
She remained dubious of his promises.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I am dubious for his story. ➜ ✅ I am dubious about his story.

data.definition: Physical harm caused to something in such a way as to impair its value, usefulness, or normal function.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'damage TO' takes 'to'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'damage' which takes NO preposition.
examples: The storm caused severe damage to several coastal homes.
Smoking causes long-term damage to your health.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The accident caused damage of my car. ➜ ✅ The accident caused damage to my car.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'damage TO the vehicle' ➔ Verb: 'damage the vehicle' (no prep)

data.definition: The possibility of suffering harm or injury.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'danger OF' before a risk event or gerund. Contrast with adjective 'dangerous for'.
examples: Drivers were warned about the danger of ice on the roads.
Is there any danger of an explosion?
data.common_mistake: ❌ The danger for slipping. ➜ ✅ The danger of slipping.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the danger OF collapse' ➔ Adjective: 'dangerous for'

data.definition: A process of becoming smaller or fewer.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'decrease IN' before the subject dropping.
examples: The company reported a decrease in quarterly revenue.
A gradual decrease in temperature signals autumn.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A decrease of unemployment. ➜ ✅ A decrease in unemployment.

data.definition: The quality of being committed to a task or purpose.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'dedicated to'. Followed by noun or gerund.
examples: Her dedication to teaching earned her a national award.
We admire his total dedication to his family.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Dedication for medicine. ➜ ✅ Dedication to medicine.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'dedication TO public service' ➔ Adjective: 'dedicated to'

data.definition: A lack or shortage of something necessary.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'short of'. Use 'deficiency IN' an area, or 'deficiency OF' a substance.
examples: A severe deficiency in iron leads to anemia.
Inspectors found structural deficiency of maintenance.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A deficiency for calcium. ➜ ✅ A deficiency in calcium.

data.definition: The desire of purchasers, consumers, or clients for a commodity or service.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'demand FOR' takes 'for'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'demand' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: There is a growing demand for renewable energy technology.
High demand for tickets crashed the website.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The demand of organic food is rising. ➜ ✅ The demand for organic food is rising.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'high demand FOR energy' ➔ Verb: 'demand' (no prep)

data.definition: The state of relying on or being controlled by someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'depend' (depend on) and adjective 'dependent on'.
examples: Reducing our dependence on foreign oil is a national priority.
Childhood involves total dependence on parents.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Dependence from computers. ➜ ✅ Dependence on computers.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'dependence ON fossil fuels' ➔ Verb: 'depend' ➔ Adjective: 'dependent on'

data.definition: The obtaining or developing of something from a source.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'derived from'. Always use 'derivation FROM'.
examples: Etymology traces the derivation of words from ancient roots.
The chemical's derivation from natural gas is documented.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Derivation of Latin. ➜ ✅ Derivation from Latin.

data.definition: A strong feeling of wanting to have something or wishing for something to happen.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'desire FOR' before nouns.
examples: Her intense desire for knowledge drove her studies.
He showed no desire for power.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A desire of money. ➜ ✅ A desire for money.

data.definition: A point or way in which things or people are not the same.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'difference BETWEEN' two entities. Contrast with adjective 'different from'.
examples: What is the main difference between these two software versions?
There is a noticeable difference in quality.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The difference from option A and B. ➜ ✅ The difference between option A and B.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the difference BETWEEN the two' ➔ Adjective: 'different from'

data.definition: The state or condition of being difficult; effort required.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'difficulty WITH' a noun/task, and 'difficulty IN' + gerund (-ing).
examples: He experiences difficulty with English pronunciation.
She had great difficulty in finding an apartment.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I have difficulty to understand this rule. ➜ ✅ I have difficulty in understanding this rule.

data.definition: An unfavorable circumstance or condition that reduces success.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'OF' after 'disadvantage'.
examples: A major disadvantage of living downtown is noise pollution.
Consider the disadvantages of taking a loan.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The disadvantage for buying cheap shoes. ➜ ✅ The disadvantage of buying cheap shoes.

data.definition: A lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'discrepancy BETWEEN'.
examples: Auditors discovered a major discrepancy between cash receipts and sales records.
Why is there a discrepancy between your stories?
data.common_mistake: ❌ A discrepancy with the figures. ➜ ✅ A discrepancy between the figures.

data.definition: The action or state of paying no attention to something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'disregard FOR' rules, safety, or authority.
examples: His total disregard for safety rules resulted in his dismissal.
The driver showed reckless disregard for pedestrians.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Disregard to the law. ➜ ✅ Disregard for the law.

data.definition: A feeling of uncertainty or lack of conviction.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'doubt ABOUT' or 'doubt OF'.
examples: I have serious doubts about the accuracy of his report.
There is no doubt about her technical ability.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Doubts for his honesty. ➜ ✅ Doubts about his honesty.

data.definition: To have courage or challenge someone.
examples: He dares to speak against injustice.
She dared him to jump into lake.
Nobody has dared to question him.

data.definition: To handle, distribute, or trade.
examples: He deals with customer complaints daily.
She dealt the cards to the players.
We have dealt with similar issues.

data.definition: To take action to handle, resolve, or cope with a situation or person.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb. Requires 'with' after 'deal'.
examples: Customer service representatives deal with complaints every day.
How do you deal with stress at work?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Deal about the issue. ➔ ✅ Deal with the issue.

data.definition: To make a choice or resolution.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'on' or 'about' when settling a matter.
examples: We decided on a location.
They are deciding about the date.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Decide on to go home. ➔ ✅ Decide to go home.

data.definition: To carefully discuss or consider a issue or decision.
data.grammar_rule: Can take a direct object or 'on'/'over' before the subject of deliberation.
examples: The jury deliberated on the verdict for three days.
The committee is deliberating over the proposed policy.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Deliberate about the verdict for days. ➔ ✅ Deliberate on the verdict.

data.definition: To ask for something authoritatively or forcefully.
data.grammar_rule: Verb takes a direct object without preposition. Noun 'demand' takes 'for'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'They demand higher wages' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'There is a high demand FOR workers' (uses FOR)
examples: Workers demand fair compensation.
The customer demanded an immediate refund.
data.common_mistake: ❌ They demanded for an answer. ➔ ✅ They demanded an answer.

data.definition: To be controlled, decided, or influenced by someone or something else.
data.grammar_rule: Always requires the preposition 'on' (or formal 'upon') before a noun or gerund object.
examples: Our weekend plans depend on the weather.
Children depend on their parents for love and security.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It depends of the situation. ➔ ✅ It depends on the situation.

data.definition: To cease or stop doing something.
data.grammar_rule: Formal inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: The court ordered them to desist from illegal activities.
They desisted from further protests after the meeting.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Desist to take action. ➔ ✅ Desist from taking action.

data.definition: To depart from an established course, standard, or topic.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'from'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Deviate from protocol' ➔ Noun: 'A deviation FROM protocol'
examples: The pilot had to deviate from the planned flight path due to weather.
We must not deviate from our original budget.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Do not deviate to the protocol. ➔ ✅ Do not deviate from the protocol.

data.definition: To stop living or cease to exist.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'die of' for disease and 'die from' for external factors.
examples: He died of old age.
Plants die from lack of water.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He died from old age. ➔ ✅ He died of old age.

data.definition: To be unlike or distinct in nature or quality.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb requiring 'from' when comparing differences between entities.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'It differs from that' ➔ Noun: 'There is a difference FROM that'
examples: British English differs from American English in vocabulary.
His second novel differs significantly from his first.
data.common_mistake: ❌ This model differs to the old one. ➔ ✅ This model differs from the old one.

data.definition: To break up and turn earth.
examples: The dog digs holes in the garden.
He dug a deep trench for the pipes.
They have dug a new well.

data.definition: To treat someone unfairly based on category, or distinguish between things.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'against' for unfair prejudice, and 'between' when making a distinction.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Discriminate against minority' ➔ Noun: 'Discrimination AGAINST minority'
examples: Laws prohibit employers from discriminating against job applicants.
Can you discriminate between genuine and fake notes?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Discriminate to elderly workers. ➔ ✅ Discriminate against elderly workers.

data.definition: To talk about something in detail with someone.
data.grammar_rule: Strictly transitive direct verb! Do NOT add 'about' after 'discuss'.
examples: We need to discuss the new budget in tomorrow's meeting.
They discussed the problem openly.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We discussed about the project. ➔ ✅ We discussed the project.

data.definition: To get rid of, throw away, or sell something.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition requiring 'of' (NEVER use 'off'!).
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Dispose of waste safely' ➔ Noun: 'Waste disposal (no prep)'
examples: Hazardous chemicals must be disposed of carefully.
The business disposed of its non-core assets.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Dispose off toxic waste. ➔ ✅ Dispose of toxic waste.

data.definition: To plunge headfirst into water.
examples: She dives off high springboard.
He dove into cold ocean waves.
They have dived for sunken treasures.

data.definition: To perform or carry out an action.
examples: She does her homework after dinner.
He did a great job on the presentation.
We have done all the work.

data.definition: To produce a picture using a pen or pencil.
examples: He draws portraits in his free time.
She drew a beautiful flower on paper.
He has drawn a detailed map.

data.definition: To experience thoughts while sleeping.
examples: She dreams of traveling the world.
He dreamt about flying last night.
I have dreamt of this moment.

data.definition: To put on clothes.
data.grammar_rule: Often used as 'get dressed'.
examples: Get dressed quickly.
She was dressed in white.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Get dressed by fast. ➔ ✅ Get dressed quickly.

data.definition: To swallow liquid.
examples: She drinks two liters of water daily.
He drank a glass of milk before bed.
We have drunk all the orange juice.

data.definition: To operate and control a vehicle.
examples: He drives to work every morning.
She drove to the beach last Sunday.
They have driven across the country.

data.definition: To quit a course, school, or competition before completion.
data.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb.
examples: He dropped out of university to start his own software company.
Injuries forced two runners to drop out of the marathon.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Dropped out the school. ➔ ✅ Dropped out of school.

data.definition: To reside or live in a place.
examples: Monks dwell in remote monastery.
She dwelt in mountain village years.
They have dwelt in peace together.

data.definition: To think or speak about a painful subject at length.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: There is no point in dwelling on past mistakes.
Try not to dwell on negative thoughts.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Don't dwell in your failures. ➔ ✅ Don't dwell on your failures.
